data.why: The app loads its own cached data (data/results.json, data/hadejia_discharge_monthly.csv, data/conecuh_discharge.csv, data/conecuh_rainfall.csv, data/conecuh_gage_height_raw.csv) already committed in the repo; it has no upload control, so nothing needs to be supplied.

goals: Read off the ARIMA model fitted to the Hadejia River's 26-year discharge record and check its residual diagnostics (Ljung-Box, ARCH)
Generate a synthetic multi-trace discharge record (e.g. 100 years x 20 traces) and compare its distribution and flow-duration curve to the measured record
Read off design flows for 2- to 500-year return periods from the pooled annual maxima of the generated record
Check which of the seven hydrological properties (mean, std, skew, lag-1 ACF, seasonal amplitude, dry-spell length, peak) the model's ensemble reproduces against held-out data
Understand, via the Documentation page, why seasonal standardisation is used instead of seasonal differencing to deseasonalise the series before fitting

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately (long synthetic records from a short gauge record, design flows read from them, a check of the model, and why standardisation beats differencing). Its evidence and its not_done notes on bugs and the doc-vs-app contradiction are careful and verified. It needs small structural fixes before filing: t2 is in the wrong phase, two toolbar-level tasks should be folded into others, f5 is oversized and should be split with property validation as its own feature, and the model-summary card and interpretation caveats are missing.
